note: Item counts established by looking at each photograph with every proposal numbered on it, and judging each one. Only photographs where a person can actually count are here. On a dense Trader Joe's haul or a filled trolley the true number is not knowable from the image, and guessing at it would produce a metric with no ground under it.
counted_by: manual review of numbered overlays, one pass
product: one purchasable unit. A twin-pack of peanut butter is two jars because they are sold and scanned as two; a six-pack of ale is one carrier because it is sold as one. A napkin holder is not a product.

counted.note: Tofu, whole chilli, rice noodles, wasabi, spring onions, ginger, mango. Seven proposals, seven items, one each. Nothing missed and nothing invented.

Two Skippy jars, hummus tub, sun-dried tomato dip, bananas. Nine proposals: all five items found, plus a napkin holder that is not a product and three boxes drawn around parts of items already proposed.

Wine, yogurt tub, protein carton, two oranges, a small bottle, a six-pack. Twelve proposals: all seven found, plus three individual bottle necks inside the six-pack and a box around the illustration on the carton.

not_countable.why: dense haul, items behind items, true count not knowable from the image
filled trolley photographed from one side
distant and low resolution, individual products not resolvable
